entry.title: Second spacewalk for CSA astronaut Joshua Kutryk
entry.summary: Earlier today, Canadian Space Agency (CSA) astronaut Colonel Joshua Kutryk conducted the second spacewalk of his career alongside NASA astronaut Anil Menon, just seven days after their previous extravehicular activity on October 29. With today's six hours and 59 minutes spacewalk that led to the installation of another solar array, the upgrade campaign launched in 2021 to enhance the Station's power generation capacity is now complete. This technology, first tested less than a decade ago, is now helping power more scientific research aboard the International Space Station and extending its operational capabilities, while also informing solar power systems that could support future missions.

entry.title: Watch live! CSA astronaut Joshua Kutryk's second spacewalk
entry.summary: On November 5, CSA astronaut Joshua Kutryk and NASA astronaut Anil Menon will venture outside the International Space Station to install the eighth and final rollout solar array of an upgrade campaign that began in 2021. This spacewalk comes one week after the pair completed a similar 7-hour-and-11-minute operation on October 29.
